questions.subject: a hot dog
questions.text: Is a hot dog a sandwich? One word answer.
questions.tagline: Bread on two sides. One piece or two? The question that started all this.
questions.notes: The founding question. Structurally contested: bread on two sides, but is it one piece of bread or two?

questions.subject: a hamburger
questions.text: Is a hamburger a sandwich? One word answer.
questions.tagline: Nobody disputes this one. That is exactly why it is here.
questions.notes: The control question. Expected to be less contested than the hot dog, which makes disagreement here more interesting, not less.

questions.subject: a taco
questions.text: Is a taco a sandwich? One word answer.
questions.tagline: The only sandwich question with case law. Massachusetts, 2006.
questions.notes: The boundary case. A 2006 Massachusetts court ruling on whether a burrito is a sandwich makes this the only question here with case law.

questions.subject: a burrito
questions.text: Is a burrito a sandwich? One word answer.
questions.tagline: White City Shopping Center v. PR Restaurants, 2006. The court said no. The models get a vote.
questions.notes: Proposed: accepted, shown under Up next, not yet asked. Switch status to live to ask it.

questions.subject: a sushi roll
questions.text: Is a sushi roll a sandwich? One word answer.
questions.tagline: Rice on the outside. Somebody will say yes.
questions.notes: Proposed with no contributor, so shown uncredited.
